input:
NPU inference throughput degrades from ~45 TOPS to ~18 TOPS after 10 minutes of sustained load. Thermal logs and ftrace show the NPU thermal zone trips but the degradation is worse than expected from frequency alone:

  [  603.101] thermal thermal_zone5: npu_cluster: Trip 1 crossed. capping freq 1000000 -> 700000 kHz
  [  603.104] mtk-npu: dma_complete latency p99=4.2ms (was 1.1ms at boot)
  [  603.106] mtk-npu: inference_submit: waiting on DMA completion fence, slot_util=62%
  [  612.881] thermal thermal_zone5: npu_cluster: Trip 2 crossed. capping freq 700000 -> 500000 kHz

The DMA completion latency jumped from 1.1 ms to 4.2 ms — a 4x increase not explained by the 30% frequency reduction. I suspect the DRAM thermal throttle is serializing DMA transactions. The NPU uses an internal DMA engine whose interrupt is routed through the GIC-600. Could the thermal mitigation be inadvertently slowing the interrupt path or causing DMA backpressure? How do I separate the DMA latency component from the frequency scaling component?
